chunks: 1956 - And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever provides iftar in this month to a believing person who is fasting, there shall be for him by that, with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness for what has passed of his sins.”

So it was said to him: “O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to provide iftar to a fasting person.” So he said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Generous; He gives this reward among you to one who is not able except for a sip of milk by which he gives a fasting person iftar, or a drink of sweet water, or a few dates; he is not able to do more than that.”

key_terms.شَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ عَذْبٍ: a drink of fresh, pleasant water
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: the reward equivalent to freeing a slave
key_terms.فَطَّرَ: provided iftar; gave food or drink for breaking the fast
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا صَائِمًا: a believing person who is fasting
key_terms.هَذَا الشَّهْرِ: this month; the blessed month being referred to in the hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving iftar to a fasting believer in this month?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages giving iftar to a believing fasting person in the month of fasting, promising immense reward and forgiveness from Allah. It also teaches that even a very small offering, such as milk, water, or a few dates, can attain this reward when one lacks the means to give more.
